title: Drift Wood #37 · the back page, last
logline: The penultimate issue. Chloe lays out the last back page she'll ever give him.

panels.composition: The newsroom. The paste-up board for the final issue. CHLOE taping the rectangle. Same gesture as #4. WOOD watching. Same.

characters.pose: taping a rectangle to the board

balloons.text: Back page. Bottom half. Last one.

image.prompt: a teenage girl taping a blank rectangle onto a newspaper paste-up board while a boy in an overcoat watches, school newsroom, the same scene as two years before
image.notes: Compose as a repeat of #4 panel 1. The reader should feel the rhyme.

balloons.text: What happens to the back page after.
Someone else edits it. Danny Voss, probably. He'll fill it with ads.

image.prompt: close-up of a teenage boy in an overcoat asking a quiet question

panels.composition: Chloe stepping back from the board. The rectangle blank.

balloons.text: I know. I'm the one who read them.

image.prompt: a teenage girl stepping back from a paste-up board with a blank rectangle taped to it, a boy beside her

panels.composition: Wood alone at the board. He draws, in the corner of the rectangle, the gull — and beside it, small, a crab. The first time both.

characters.pose: drawing in the corner of the rectangle

props: rectangle with a gull and a crab in the corner

image.prompt: a teenage boy alone leaning over a paste-up board drawing a tiny gull and a tiny crab in the corner of an empty rectangle, newsroom lamp
image.notes: Both marks. The margin below carries only the crab; the gull-and-crab is inside the panel.

notes: Rhymes with #4. Both marks drawn inside the panel; the margin keeps the crab.
